answer.label: Widely attributed to
answer.sourceLine: This wording is widely credited to Jiddu Krishnamurti, but his Foundation Trust expressly says that it cannot authenticate the exact words. It documents similar ideas in his talks, which is different from establishing this sentence as a verbatim quotation.

author.name: Jiddu Krishnamurti
author.heading: About Jiddu Krishnamurti
author.bio: Jiddu Krishnamurti spoke internationally about psychological conditioning, freedom and the observation of thought. Having rejected the spiritual authority prepared for him by the Theosophical movement, he urged people to examine experience without depending on a teacher or organization.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The Foundation places the popular line beside actual discussions of social conditioning, loneliness and psychological conflict. Those passages explain why it sounds consistent with Krishnamurti’s concerns, while the Foundation’s explicit caution prevents treating consistency of thought as proof of exact wording.

schema.faqAnswer: The attribution is not confirmed. Krishnamurti Foundation Trust says it cannot attribute these exact words to him, although it documents similar ideas in his talks.
